column1: # The payload register. ONE file, shared by seven repositories, read by
# `nmg2_tools/payload_lint.py`; that module's docstring is the authority on
# what each field means and this header does not restate it.
#     <path><TAB><visibility><TAB><home>[<TAB>pending=<reason>]
# `home` is REQUIRED on every row and lists, comma-separated, the repositories
# where the row is EXPECTED TO MATCH a committed path. It is not a scope: a
# `public` row still registers its path wherever the path turns up. It is
# where the row is CHECKED. In a home repository a row that matches nothing is
# `PAYLOAD-REGISTER-UNMATCHED`, which is the finding that did not exist while
# six rows in this file asserted a provenance for paths that were not there --
# five under a `g2Lib/` root the tree has never had, and one, `frame_sync_spin.asm`,
# naming a file that has never existed in `gearmulator` on any branch. Nothing
# reported them because a row matching nothing by accident and a row whose file
# has not landed yet looked identical. The `home` field and the `pending=`
# marker are what tells them apart, IN THE DATA, so only the deliberate one can
# be quiet.
# A home slug must appear in `KNOWN_REPOSITORIES`, so a typo cannot move out of
# the path field and into the home field and go on asserting nothing.
nmg2_tools/testdata/pch2_synth/
# `gearmulator` test fixtures. THE PREFIX ON THESE FIVE ROWS WAS WRONG AND THE
# ROWS GRANTED NOTHING. `g2Lib/` is where the library sits inside its own
# subtree; the repository-relative path -- the only thing `git ls-files` emits
# and the only thing this register matches -- is `source/nord/g2/g2Lib/`. All
# five rows were exact-path rows, so each compared unequal against every
# committed file and no `PAYLOAD-UNREGISTERED` finding was ever answered by
# one. `git ls-files | grep -Fxc <row>` returns 0 for each of the five.
# Nothing reported this, because a row that matches no path is indistinguishable
# from a row that matches a path which is absent. The rows were written in
# a91909d and the guard had never run on a pull request in `gearmulator` until
# the `pull_request` trigger landed, so the first run to read them was also the
# first run that could have contradicted them.
# The correction is the prefix, applied to the class and not case by case: one
# root was wrong for all five, which is a predicate and not a roster.
# `esai_sync_spin.asm` REPLACES the row that read `frame_sync_spin.asm`. No file
# of that name exists in `gearmulator`, on any branch, at any point in its
# history -- `git ls-files` and `git log --all -S frame_sync_spin` both return
# nothing, against a known positive of 1 for `esai_sync_spin` from the same
# command. The row named a file that never landed; the file that did land came
# in f0854094 for task SCH-34.
# PROVENANCE, established per file from the introducing commit and the file's
# own content, not assumed -- a `public` row asserts a provenance, so guessing
# one would be worse than the red it quiets. The three `.asm` files are
# hand-authored DSP56300 spins of two, four and twenty-five instructions,
# built from `nop`, `bra`, `brclr` and `move`, each majority prose comment
# describing what the check that reads it asserts. Nothing here is disassembled
# output. `synth_editor_sequence.txt` holds no payload bytes: it is one row per
# frame carrying an index, a type code, a length and a CRC-16 over the payload,
# and the corpus it describes is `nmg2_tools/testdata/pch2_synth/` above, whose
# generator states that every byte of it is authored by this project.

# Each row below names ONE tree, and is a decision on the record about that tree
# and nothing else. Together they answer most of the PAYLOAD-UNREGISTERED
# backlog these repositories carried; the alternative that clears the same
# ground in one line -- "exempt anything present at the upstream fork point" --
# was measured and REJECTED. It exempts by history rather than by content, so it
# cannot see a file arriving by another route; it makes the verdict depend on a
# fetched remote ref that moves between CI runs; and it exempts by an attribute
# a reviewer reading this file cannot see. A row per tree costs more than one
# line and keeps all three properties, which is the correct price.
# Writing these rows made clause 3 READABLE for the first time, and it answered
# 389 times: files above the ceiling in trees this project did not author. Every
# one of the 389 is present in the upstream tree at the fork point and NONE was
# added by this fork [MEASURED 2026-08-27; `comm` of each repository's ceiling
# finding paths against `git ls-tree -r --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD
# upstream/main)`; one unit is one finding line]. They are upstream's GUI skins,
# fonts, gettext catalogues, sample media and generated ABI descriptions. The
# largest are two 19 MB Photoshop sources for a plugin's demo background and a
# 14.8 MB wxWidgets `.abi`, all authored upstream in 2022-2024.
# So the rows below split, and the split is what the measurement says and not a
# preference. A tree MEASURED to carry inherited bulk is `allow-listed`, because
# a tree we did not author and do not review line by line is one whose asset
# sizes are upstream's decision, and repeating that verdict 389 times as file
# rows would be the roster this file exists to avoid. A tree measured to carry
# NONE is left `public`, and clause 3 still weighs every non-source file
# beneath it -- so the first large blob to appear in `source/fst/`,
# `source/3rdparty/`, `source/HxDplugin/`, `source/vtuneSdk/` or `Musashi/` is
# PAYLOAD-CEILING and someone has to decide about it.
# WHAT `allow-listed` GIVES UP, stated rather than implied: inside the nine
# trees that carry it, a new over-ceiling non-source file no longer fails. That
# is the price of not writing 389 rows, and it is bounded -- it buys nothing for
# clause 1, which still refuses a `.pch2` beneath any of these rows because a
# `public allow-listed` row is not a `pch2-exception` row; it buys nothing for
# clause 2, so a new vendored tree is still PAYLOAD-UNREGISTERED until someone
# writes its row; and it buys nothing outside the named tree.
# Third-party libraries, vendored into these forks upstream.
# `wxWidgets` carries 204 over-ceiling files, `portaudio` 5, `portmidi` 5 and
# `libresample` 1; the other three carry none and stay tight.
